method: Same Ryzen 9 9900X / RTX 5060 Ti, nine-stone start, 49 inventory stones, seed 0, 1024 iterations, unmodified apps/excavator/config/mcts_cuda.yml, one BLAS/OpenMP thread, sequential fresh processes, search-only timing. Before is the vectorized-sampling run (excavator-mcts-vectorized-sampling.json). Native work was screened by replaying all 26 solve_batch calls (2627 jobs, 9327 native job-stages) captured from that search through a fresh CudaPlacementPoseSolver; replay times are the best of 2-3 repeats and the digest covers every returned pose, cost, status and diagnostic.
changes: stacking-apps: CudaPlacementPoseSolver.batch_size 128 -> 256, so a 256-node generation batch is one chunk per schedule stage.
stacking-core pose_graph.cu: queries kernel uses one warp per job; ballot ranks keep the serial query slot and queue order.
stacking-core queries.cu: posegen support, contact and Hausdorff queues drain in one launch (independent result slots).

stacking-core pose_generator.cpp: once at most 64 force jobs remain, one tail launch runs all remaining sweeps; each block stops at its job's own convergence/limit, removing per-32-sweep progress readbacks.

replay.step: capacity 512 (not adopted; batches never exceed 256 jobs)
+ single tail launch for the remaining force sweeps

nsight_replay.note: nsys -t cuda --cuda-graph-trace=node on one replay; device kernel durations, memcpy API call counts (blocking pageable readbacks).
